findings.summary: Section 3 lists 'serde DTO decoding' under Not performed. Yet r2 performs closed-key checks (12/29/export field names) and integer-width checks that are the Python analogue of serde deny_unknown_fields typed decoding. 'Each ... mirrors a named check' also maps the EXPORT-stage hex-width checks only onto later Rust equality comparisons. This is wording imprecision, not an admission-relation claim.
findings.evidence: S33 §3 'Not performed: ... serde DTO decoding' versus CP02/CP03/CI05 closed schemas and u8/u16/u64 ranges. S18 SetupRecord/ProofExport #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] decoded inside parse_json (S28). S18 check_export validates programHash, setupRecordSha256 and context hex only through same()/equality. The 'Added by r2' list already covers sourceSha256-key-required (the Option→None serde difference) and the exact-int rules.
findings.requiredFix: Non-blocking. In test-review notes or a later text revision, say that serde mechanics (Option-missing→None, numeric coercion, UTF-8 decoding) are not reproduced, and that the closed-key and width checks are r2 Python analogues. No clause change or re-vote is needed.

findings.summary: The CP04 scan constraints (no input-proportional copy, never str.encode, length-before-scan for abi2ShapeBytesHex/statementHex) cannot be discriminated by T00-T17 outcomes. T06 detects only wrong stages and subclass leaks, and an implementation that catches UnicodeEncodeError and re-raises ValueError would pass every test.
findings.evidence: S33 CP04 and stage notes; T06/T15 rows; the meaningfulness list covers only a no-scan mutant. The T15 token scan reuses v1 test_11 tokens (S23), which do not include 'encode('.
findings.requiredFix: The test reviewer and the later implementation reviewer must source-inspect these constraints. Optionally add '.encode(' to the T15 effect-token scan, since r2 needs no encode call. Non-blocking.

So 'stale' is scoped history, not exact-byte provenance.
